ops.title: ccx vcs history <dir> scopes each commit's diff to one arbitrary file in the directory
ops.description:
`internal/cli/history.go:111` sets `c.path = r.Entries[len(r.Entries)-1].New` —
always a single file, because `git log --name-status` names files, never
directories. So when a user runs `ccx vcs history sub`, the commit's stat line is
scoped to whichever file happened to be LAST in that commit's name-status output,
not to the directory.

Consequence: `commitStat`'s pathspec (`history.go:151`) is structurally always a
file. A side effect is that `vcs.NumstatRecord.Old` — git's rename pre-image — is
unreachable from this call site, since a file pathspec filters the pre-image
deletion out before rename detection runs. Measured against real git 2.55:
`git show --numstat --format=%P -z HEAD -- new.txt` on a pure `git mv` commit
returns a plain add; only a DIRECTORY pathspec (`-- sub`) yields the rename
record `0\t0\t\0sub/old.txt\0sub/new.txt\0`.

The parser handles it correctly either way — `internal/vcs/gitrun_test.go:589`
covers the rename record directly — so this is a product question about what a
directory argument should mean, not a parsing defect.

Pre-existing; surfaced 2026-08-03 during the history centralization lane, which
correctly declined to change behavior.

ops.text: Decide whether a directory argument should report the directory's aggregate churn or per-file churn, and implement it
